parts:
Luxury businesses should keep AI agents away from unsupervised client communication. Start with jewellery service drafts, with a person approving every send.

→ Anthropic's third-quarter revenue rose 45% to $16.8 billion; supplier growth offers no assurance that agents can safely handle client communication.

→ Richemont and Signet Jewelers are in talks to join a consortium bidding for De Beers; a deal would link jewellery retailers more closely to diamond supply.

→ M&S has added Klarna to its website and app for three equal, interest-free payments; shoppers gain more flexibility at checkout.

Read, listen or watch the full issue, free every Monday: https://luxury-intel.com/digest/october-2026-week-42?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=2026-W42&utm_content=issue-post

#retailtech #jewelry #ecommerce
LVMH's fashion sales are falling while Brunello Cucinelli raises its targets. China has become an easy excuse for weak brands.
Richemont and Signet are in talks to join a consortium bidding for De Beers, Bloomberg reports. A purchase would connect jewellery retail more closely with diamond mining.
M&S has added Klarna to its website and app. Shoppers can split purchases into three equal, interest-free payments. That reduces the amount customers need to pay upfront.
Anthropic's third-quarter revenue rose 45% to $16.8 billion. Growth offers no assurance that agents can safely handle clients. Jewellery service replies should require human approval before sending.
Read, listen or watch the full issue, free every Monday: https://luxury-intel.com/digest/october-2026-week-42?utm_source=x&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=2026-W42&utm_content=thread
LVMH fashion sales fell 5% as Chinese demand weakened. The group found growth in selective retailing, home to Sephora, where sales rose 8%.
Ikea has launched a flagship store on Douyin in China, giving shoppers a route from short videos to purchases within ByteDance’s platform.
LVMH’s jewellery segment revenue rose 8% in the third quarter. Luxury retailers have a positive sales benchmark for the category.
ASML expects to fall short of AI-driven customer demand in 2027 and 2028. Retailers setting long-term AI budgets should factor in the risk of supply constraints.
